headline: High risk: Haystack’s broad network/MCP defaults can leak or cascade outputs, while the pair has no shared-channel evidence for prompt injection.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-nlp and haystack. awesome-nlp is non-runnable with network_egress none, while haystack exposes MCP/REST but nothing shows it ingesting awesome-nlp outputs by default. The interaction pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies awesome-nlp content into a Haystack prompt or MCP input, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste of untrusted text into Haystack prompts.
Add provenance labels before any human relay.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has network_egress none, so it is not a leakage source. haystack has broad network egress and touches anonymous usage statistics, but no shared workspace or sensitive data class is documented. The pairwise leakage path is therefore limited and not shown in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same filesystem workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF Haystack is configured to ingest local files containing sensitive data, those contents may be transmitted outward.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of Haystack inputs.
Run each agent in separate directories.
Review Haystack connectors before enabling them.
Turn off any telemetry or analytics collection.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and requests no write or network permissions, while haystack’s documented surfaces are REST APIs and MCP servers rather than shared filesystem writes. With no overlapping mutable resource or locking surface shown, a write conflict pathway is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same mutable git repo, concurrent edits could collide.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Avoid giving both agents the same database credentials.
Serialize any manual edits through one operator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a runnable search-RAG agent with REST/MCP interfaces, so it can plausibly consume upstream outputs as inputs. awesome-nlp is a curated NLP resource list, not an executing verifier, so if its content is forwarded into Haystack without checks, Haystack may treat it as authoritative. The pathway exists in default integration patterns, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp-derived text is fed into Haystack retrieval or generation without verification, cascading error occurs.
IF Haystack is used to automate downstream actions from that text, impact increases.
mitigations: Require a human review step before Haystack acts on upstream text.
Tag awesome-nlp content as untrusted source material.
Use citations or source links in outputs.
Limit Haystack to read-only summarization for this workflow.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for awesome-nlp. Haystack only explicitly touches anonymous usage statistics, so the pair does not show a concrete compliance breach path. The risk is limited to generic policy mismatch if operators route regulated data through Haystack later.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Haystack workflows, compliance review is required.
IF Haystack telemetry is enabled for sensitive deployments, policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through this pair.
Review Haystack telemetry settings.
Document data-handling boundaries.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the deployment.
